findings.title: Published current-cycle evidence still cannot satisfy its own freshness gate
findings.evidence: The acceptance row still claims 307/307 tests and contains no literal "current cycle totals:" tag. The live checker requires exactly that tagged public-web/editor-core pattern and exits 1 when absent. implementation.json instead reports 349/349 public-web and 68/68 editor-core, while delivery-gates.json nevertheless marks acceptance evidence passed. This directly regresses review-006, -007, -008, -009, -010, and -012.

implementation_guidance.approach: Run both final test suites, publish their exact totals in the canonical acceptance row using the checker's required tag, then regenerate summary, design-system status, provenance, handoff, and delivery gates in dependency order. Do not let a structural completeness check stand in for the executable freshness check.

findings.title: Dirty Back/Forward behavior is not exercised through a real browser history traversal
findings.evidence: All three tests call history.pushState to place the window at the destination and then manually dispatch PopStateEvent. They never call history.back(), history.forward(), or history.go(), and therefore cannot exercise Next App Router's competing history listener, component lifecycle, traversal timing, or query-bearing editor URLs. No browser artifact covers this critical data-loss guard, despite review-012 explicitly requiring browser coverage when jsdom cannot model Next history faithfully.
findings.expected_fix: Verify dirty Back/Forward cancel, confirm, and saved behavior using real browser history traversal.

implementation_guidance.approach: Add a browser-level scenario that creates same-origin history entries around the editor, dirties the document, invokes actual Back and Forward traversal, and observes the existing confirmation flow. Include a query-template editor URL so cancellation proves the complete editor URL and state remain intact.
tests: Dirty history.back() shows confirmation and cancel preserves document plus full editor URL.
Confirming dirty Back/Forward reaches the captured destination.
Exercise /tao-thiep?template=<id> and both backward and forward directions.
done_when: Evidence uses actual browser traversal rather than a fabricated event.
Cancel, confirm, saved, query-string, backward, and forward variants pass under the real Next runtime.
No dirty traversal can unmount or lose editor state before confirmation.

findings.title: Canvas export can rasterize fallback fonts before self-hosted fonts are ready
findings.evidence: renderPageToCanvas immediately preloads images and starts measuring/drawing text. It never awaits document.fonts.ready or document.fonts.load for the selected next/font families. Canvas pixels do not update when a font later finishes loading. The browser smoke selects fonts early and performs many operations before export; it only asserts the assigned ctx.font string and eventual pixel parity, so it cannot detect an immediate or delayed-font export race.
findings.expected_fix: Wait for every required text face to be available before irreversible canvas measurement and drawing.

implementation_guidance.approach: Before drawing, collect distinct font/style/weight specifications used by visible text and await the FontFaceSet for those faces, with explicit unsupported-browser and load-failure behavior. Keep image and font preload failures honest rather than silently reporting a correct export.
tests: Unit-test that text drawing waits for a controllable FontFaceSet promise.
Browser-test export immediately after selecting a font while its response is artificially delayed.
Verify normal, bold, italic, and multiple distinct fonts still match the live renderer.
done_when: No text measureText/fillText call occurs before its selected font load settles.
A delayed-font browser case downloads pixels using the selected self-hosted face, not fallback glyphs.
Font-load failure produces an explicit supported outcome and never a false success.

findings.title: No-op commands still create undo entries and can dirty the draft
findings.evidence: commit always appends next and increments historyIndex even when updater returns current. Edge movePage/deletePage calls therefore add redundant undo states. bringForward/sendBackward return an unchanged page at a z-order boundary but still return a new state/pages array, causing the autosave effect to mark the document unsaved. The corresponding UI buttons remain enabled at boundaries.
findings.expected_fix: No-op page and layer commands must preserve history, redo state, and draft status.

findings.title: A locked element still accepts rotation-only command patches
findings.evidence: The locked-element guard calls isGeometryPatch, whose GEOMETRY_KEYS contain x, y, width, and height but omit rotation. patchGroup separately recognizes rotation as geometry, and the adjacent comment promises locked elements reject drag/resize/rotate/nudge/align. The visible rotate handle is hidden when locked, but the shared command API violates its lock invariant and lacks a command-level regression test.
findings.expected_fix: Treat rotation as locked geometry in the authoritative updateElement command path.

summary: Full coverage is complete. The implementation is substantially functional and the five fidelity failures are validly waived, but it is not ready: three major issues remain—stale/self-contradictory current-cycle evidence, no real-browser verification of the dirty Back/Forward guard, and an export race that can rasterize fallback fonts. Two lower-impact history/lock invariants also remain. The final architecture knowledge proposal is not approved because it still says persisted blob: URLs are allowed, contradicting the corrected canonical validator.
